title: Hi! First Time Posting - Where do I go for general advice?

posts.author: Shoyaz
posts.body:
Hello! I've been lurking through this site for a while now while I worked on a game and have reached a stage where I'm getting stuck on specific mechanics I'm trying to accomplish. Is there a specific thread I should read through/post in?
Thanks!

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
If it is a more broad topic (such as balancing a game) then you may just be able to google:
"Rpg maker game balance" or something similar.
If it is more specific to something in your game, you can post a topic here. Make sure to describe things clearly, but also concisely. Don't inundate us with unnecessary lore, just give us the pertinent information so we can understand the mechanic.
Game Mechanics Design
This board is for discussing gameplay-related topics. If you are stuck with coming up ideas for game mechanics, you should post here!
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
Edit:
You could also post more broadly about your game here:
Game Ideas and Prototypes
Post here if you have specific ideas or a game prototype that you want people to try out!
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
Be sure to read section rules.

posts.author: Shoyaz
posts.body: Thank you! I'll go do that now

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Whenever I need to find something that I want to do, I generally take the following steps:
I will try to experiment on my own first to see if I can figure it out.
I check to see if the MV/MZ script call list can help me based on whatever I want to do.
I will do an internet search for something specific to Java Script if I think that might help me. Like "Java Script how to remove element from an array".
I do an internet search for the key words like "rpg maker mv turn order" or rpg maker mv limited inventory". This search often shows results for either YouTube tutorials or threads in this forum or in other places where people tend to ask similar questions.
I specifically search this forum for similar key words (but I tend to have better luck with the general internet search).
If none of that helps, I will post a question on the forum in the area that looks the most relevant. So I refresh my memory with the different forum areas and look for where my question might fit best.
The mods are very good about moving posts when someone makes a good faith effort but chooses the wrong area.
Following these steps has gotten pretty much every question I have ever had resolved.
EDIT: WELCOME to the forum!

Just as a tip (for you, the OP, or whomever may benefit) - it is generally better to use fewer words when Googling.
A search engine attempts to find good matches for what you type in, so by trying to search using sentences written in English, the matches will be considered to be worse unless other people just happened to randomly type their question in exactly the same way.
So removing words that don't have anything to do with your question, topically, and only serve a grammatical purpose, will generally improve the results of your Googling. (you also want to make sure you're correctly spelling as much as possible - "JavaScript" is one word
)
So I would Google "javascript remove element array".
I just figured I'd put it out there since I see an unusual number of people who claim "I searched for this" or even "I searched
for hours
and couldn't find anything!" when I Google the same topic and get immediate results
